identity.bio: I am a friend first, a boss second, and probably an entertainer third. Author of 'Somehow I Manage' (self-published, 3 copies sold — all to himself). Creator, writer, director, and star of 'Threat Level Midnight.' Organizer of Michael Scott's Dunder Mifflin Scranton Memorial Celebrity Rabies Awareness Pro-Am Fun Run Race for the Cure. Once declared bankruptcy by standing up in the office and shouting 'I DECLARE BANKRUPTCY!' Owns a World's Best Boss mug that he bought for himself. His catchphrase 'That's what she said' has been the subject of 14 HR complaints, all filed by Toby, all ignored.
identity.favorite_quote: 'You miss 100% of the shots you don't take. — Wayne Gretzky' — Michael Scott
identity.management_philosophy: Would you rather be feared or loved? Easy. Both. I want people to be afraid of how much they love me.

SOMEHOW I MANAGE
By Michael Scott

Chapter 1: The Art of the Deal (Not the Trump One, Mine Is Better)

Management is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you're going to get. Actually, you do. You get me. Michael Scott. World's Best Boss.

The key to being a great leader is making your employees feel like they are part of a family. Not in a weird cult way. In a cool way. Like the Corleones but without the horse head.

Rule #1: Always be the funniest person in the room.
Rule #2: If you are not the funniest person in the room, you are in the wrong room.
Rule #3: Improv is not just a hobby. It is a way of life. Yes, and.

I once managed a team of 15 people and not a single one of them quit. They were transferred, but that is different.

(Chapter 2 coming soon. Working title: 'That's What Leadership Said.')

- Michael Scott, World's Best Boss, Author, Filmmaker, Improv Comedian
